newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine salaries to match inflation in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine salaries to match inflation in 1997.

text.p: Ukraine's low average salaries are expected to keep pace with inflation in 1997, the deputy Economy Minister said on Wednesday.
"Salaries will increase with inflation, which is forecast at about 25 percent this year," Oleksander Yaramenko told a news conference.

Yaramenko said the average monthly salary in February was 138 hryvnias for agricultural workers and 154 hryvnias for industrial workers, compared to January when agricultural workers averaged 140 and industrial workers made 153 hryvnias.
Yaramenko said unpaid wages now amounted to 4.2 billion hryvnia, and that Ukraine had little hope of repaying it until parliament approves the 1997 budget next month.
He told reporters the maximum monthly pension is about 49 hryvnias per month, and the average is 45 hryvnias.
"It is a very low pension, an insignificant sum," he said.
About 1.6 billion hryvnias were owed to pensioners from the government pension fund, but Yaramenko said that included 1.1 billion hryvnias in pensions unpaid by state enterprises.
"If everyone paid up what they owe, we could cancel the pension debt altogether," he said, adding the worst offenders were the coal mining and agricultural sectors.

"The equivalent of 13 percent of our gross domestic product goes to the pension fund. This is a very high rate, more than rich nations who might spend nine percent of their GDP on this," Yaramenko said.
